watering_every_days.note: Check the caudex (swollen stem base) before watering; hydrate thoroughly only when the caudex feels slightly soft or the potting medium is completely bone dry. During the Indian monsoon, shelter the plant from continuous rainfall as soggy roots quickly trigger fatal caudex rot. In winter dormancy (Nov–Jan), Adenium sheds leaves and needs minimal water once every 2–3 weeks.

soil.in_simple_words: Super gritty, ultra-porous potting mix that lets water flush straight through in seconds and retains zero stagnant moisture around the caudex.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts coarse river sand/pumice + 2 parts cinder or broken brick grit + 1 part garden soil + 1 part well-decomposed cow dung or vermicompost + 1 tbsp neem cake

pet_and_child_safety.note: Extremely toxic to dogs, cats, and humans. All parts contain toxic cardiac glycosides (including oleandrin) historically used as African arrow poison. Ingestion can cause severe gastrointestinal distress, vomiting, irregular heartbeat, low blood pressure, lethargy, and even death. The milky sap also causes painful skin and eye irritation.

common_problems.problem: Caudex and root rot (Waterlogging and fungal infection)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the swollen caudex turning soft, squishy, or brown at the soil line, with leaves turning yellow and dropping rapidly?
solve_it_like_this: Immediately unpot the plant and scrape away all soft, dark, mushy tissue using a sanitized razor until only clean green-white flesh remains.
Dust the cut wounds thoroughly with systemic fungicide powder (such as Bavistin/carbendazim or Saaf) or cinnamon powder, and let it dry in shade for 5–7 days.
Repot into completely fresh, dry cinder- or grit-heavy succulent mix with zero garden clay.
Shelter from rain and withhold water for at least 10–14 days until new root bumps develop.

common_problems.problem: Spider mites and yellow oleander aphids (Pest infestation on tender tips)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see tiny bright yellow bugs clustering on shoot tips and flower buds, or fine webbing with dusty stippled leaves under the leaf undersides?
solve_it_like_this: Wash the foliage with a targeted jet of water in the morning to dislodge colonies.
Spray thoroughly with neem oil emulsion (5 ml cold-pressed neem oil + 2 ml liquid soap per litre of water) every 4–5 days.
For severe mite attacks during hot dry May weather, dust with wettable sulfur or apply a mild miticide.

common_problems.problem: Flower bud drop or blast (Sudden moisture stress or thrips)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are promising flower buds turning brown, drying up, or falling off before opening into full blooms?
solve_it_like_this: Avoid letting the pot go bone dry for too long when buds are forming in spring and summer.
Inspect petal tips for microscopic thrips; spray with mild neem spray or imidacloprid if thrips rasping is detected.
Ensure the plant receives at least 6 hours of full direct sunlight daily.

common_problems.problem: Winter dormancy defoliation (Seasonal leaf drop)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are lower and middle leaves turning uniformly yellow and falling off during November to January while the caudex remains firm and hard?
solve_it_like_this: Recognize that this is normal winter dormancy in North and Central India; the plant is conserving energy.
Drastically reduce watering to once every 2–3 weeks, only dampening the soil perimeter.
Do not apply any fertilizers or prune branches until warm spring weather arrives in February.

watering_every_days.note: Allow the top half of the potting soil to dry out thoroughly between waterings. Exceptionally resilient to prolonged dry spells, but susceptible to root rot if soil remains soggy during persistent monsoon rains. Water around the base of the stems, avoiding splashing water into the dense thorny thickets.

soil.in_simple_words: Sharp-draining, porous succulent soil that prevents water from lingering around fleshy, spiny stems.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts garden soil + 2 parts coarse sand or perlite + 1 part vermicompost + 1 part crushed brick or pumice

pet_and_child_safety.note: Highly toxic to dogs, cats, and humans. Euphorbia milii stems contain a poisonous milky latex (sap) rich in caustic phorbol esters that cause painful skin blistering, eye inflammation or temporary blindness upon contact, and intense vomiting and mouth irritation if ingested. Sharp thorns also pose a serious puncture risk.

common_problems.problem: Root and stem rot (Waterlogging in heavy clay soil)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are stems softening, turning blackish-brown at soil level, with yellowing leaves drooping despite wet soil?
solve_it_like_this: Stop watering immediately and verify that the pot's drainage holes are free of blockages.
Move the plant out of persistent monsoon rain under a covered balcony or awning.
Cut away rotted stem sections using a sterilized knife (wear protective gloves to avoid sap), allow the cuts to callus, and repot in fresh gritty soil.

common_problems.problem: Sudden leaf drop (Moisture shock or relocation stress)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are numerous green and yellow leaves dropping rapidly following sudden weather shifts or moving indoors?
solve_it_like_this: Maintain consistent watering intervals—avoid swinging between extreme bone-dry neglect and heavy flood watering.
Keep the pot in a stable, sun-drenched location receiving at least 4–5 hours of direct sun daily.
Allow the plant a couple of weeks to adapt; fresh leaves will sprout quickly once watering stabilizes.

common_problems.problem: Mealybugs (Cottony white clusters lodged between thorns)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are there fuzzy white cotton-like deposits tucked deep into stem nodes and thorn bases, attracting ants?
solve_it_like_this: Dip a cotton swab or old toothbrush in 70% isopropyl alcohol and dab directly onto mealybug clusters between the thorns.
Spray with a neem oil solution (5 ml/L) mixed with a few drops of dish soap early in the morning.
Isolate the plant to prevent the pests from spreading to nearby succulents.

common_problems.problem: Sparse flowering (Insufficient sunlight or excess nitrogen)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the plant producing healthy leafy green shoots but rarely producing its vibrant red, pink, or yellow floral bracts?
solve_it_like_this: Shift the pot to the sunniest spot on your terrace or balcony where it gets maximum unfiltered sunshine.
Switch from high-nitrogen fertilisers to a phosphorus- and potassium-rich feed like steamed bone meal or dilute banana peel tea once a month.
Prune old leggy branches in early spring to encourage compact, flower-bearing side shoots.

watering_every_days.note: Water thoroughly only after the top 5 cm (2 inches) of soil has dried out completely. Use the soak-and-dry approach, pouring water at soil level without wetting the crown or leaves. In monsoon, keep sheltered from direct downpours as lingering moisture on thick scalloped leaves triggers fungal leaf spot and stem rot.

soil.in_simple_words: Light, aerated, well-draining succulent potting mix with good grit and moderate organic matter.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts garden soil + 2 parts coarse sand or perlite + 1 part vermicompost + 1 part cocopeat or leaf mold

pet_and_child_safety.note: Toxic to dogs, cats, and birds. Contains bufadienolide cardiac glycosides. Ingesting any part, especially the vibrant flower clusters, can trigger drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and in severe cases abnormal heart rhythms and muscle weakness.

common_problems.problem: Powdery mildew (White powdery coating on foliage)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves developing a chalky white or grayish fungal powdery film, causing foliage to curl and dry out?
solve_it_like_this: Relocate the plant to a breezy spot with good indirect light and generous air movement.
Prune off heavily mildewed leaves and dispose of them properly.
Spray with a solution of baking soda (5 g/L with 2 drops liquid soap) or a sulfur-based organic fungicide.
Never mist succulent leaves or water from overhead.

common_problems.problem: Basal stem and root rot (Overwatering and poor drainage)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the lower stem turning dark and mushy at the soil line, with leaves collapsing into water-soaked pulp?
solve_it_like_this: Cease watering immediately and ensure water drains freely through the pot's bottom holes.
If the base has rotted, cut healthy top stem cuttings above the rot line, let them callus for 2 days, and root in fresh dry perlite-sand mix.
Discard waterlogged potting soil and disinfect the container before reuse.

common_problems.problem: Failure to rebloom (Lack of photoperiod dark cycle)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Does your Kalanchoe continue growing lots of lush green leaves year after year without setting new floral buds?
solve_it_like_this: Kalanchoe is a short-day plant that requires 14 hours of continuous uninterrupted darkness every night for 6 weeks (during autumn/winter) to set buds.
Cover the plant with a cardboard box or move it into a dark closet from 6 PM to 8 AM daily from October to November.
Feed with a phosphorus- and potassium-rich organic fertiliser once buds start emerging.

common_problems.problem: Leaf sunburn (Intense summer midday heat)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do fleshy leaves show dried, bleached-white or crisp brown patches on sections facing the sun?
solve_it_like_this: Move the plant behind a sheer curtain or under 50% green agro-shade netting during harsh Indian summer afternoons (11 AM to 4 PM).
Ensure it receives plenty of gentle early morning sunlight instead.
Trim severely scorched crispy leaves to encourage tidy new foliage.

watering_every_days.note: Bottom water or use a precision squeeze bottle to apply water directly to the soil, keeping the delicate rosette crown completely bone dry. During the humid Indian monsoon, withhold water until lower leaves visibly wrinkle and feel limp. Keep under a covered balcony or indoor grow light away from rain.

soil.in_simple_words: Extremely porous, mineral-heavy succulent mix with pumice, perlite, and brick grit that dries within 24 to 48 hours.
soil.mix_recipe: 3 parts pumice or volcanic cinder + 2 parts coarse silica sand or perlite + 1 part sifted garden soil + 1 part vermicompost

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic to cats, dogs, and humans according to ASPCA records. Safe for homes with curious pets, though the brittle rosette leaves snap easily if disturbed.

common_problems.problem: Etiolation and leggy stretching (Insufficient light)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the compact, tight rosette stretching out with wide gaps between leaves and turning pale light green?
solve_it_like_this: Gradually transition the succulent to a brighter spot receiving 4–6 hours of direct morning sunlight or under a full-spectrum LED grow light.
Do not move abruptly from deep shade to harsh 40°C afternoon sun or leaves will burn.
Behead the stretched rosette top, let it callus for 3 days, and replant in gritty mix to recreate a compact form.

common_problems.problem: Rosette crown rot (Water trapped in leaf cup)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the center of the rosette turning translucent, blackened, and falling apart into mush?
solve_it_like_this: Never water from above; if water accidentally splashes into the rosette center, blow it out gently with a rubber air blower or dab with tissue.
Increase ventilation immediately with an oscillating fan during humid monsoon days.
Remove rotting leaves promptly; if the central apex has rotted, save undamaged outer leaves for propagation.

common_problems.problem: Mealybugs (Cottony pests nestled deep between rosette leaves)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you notice sticky sap residue and tiny cottony white insects hidden at the base of leaves near the stem?
solve_it_like_this: Dip a fine artist's paintbrush in 70% rubbing alcohol and dab directly onto mealybugs in the crevices.
Avoid spraying oily emulsions directly on the leaves as oils dissolve the protective farina wax coating.
Drench the soil with systemic neem cake tea or a mild systemic insecticide to eradicate root mealybugs.

common_problems.problem: Damaged farina epicuticular wax (Fingerprint smudges and chemical marks)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are there dark green smudges, fingerprint marks, or patchy blotches ruining the plant's powdery silvery-blue coating?
solve_it_like_this: Avoid touching rosette leaves with bare fingers; always handle the plant by the root ball or pot rim.
Farina cannot regenerate once wiped off on older leaves, but new center leaves will grow back with a pristine powdery coating.
Protect from heavy spray droplets and overhead rain.

watering_every_days.note: Soak thoroughly only when the potting mix is dry all the way to the bottom hole. Haworthiopsis enters semi-dormancy during peak Indian summer heat (May–June) and cold winter; reduce watering during these phases to prevent stagnant moisture from destroying the root system.

soil.in_simple_words: Fast-draining gritty succulent mix with high inorganic mineral content (pumice, brick chips, sand).
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts pumice or coarse sand + 1 part perlite + 1 part potting soil + 1 part vermicompost

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic to dogs, cats, and humans (verified by ASPCA). An ideal, child-friendly and pet-safe succulent for desks, window sills, and coffee tables.

common_problems.problem: Root loss and basal rot (Overwatering and poorly drained pot)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Does the plant feel loose in the pot, with outer leaves turning soft, mushy, or translucent yellow at the base?
solve_it_like_this: Gently pull the plant from its container; shake away old soil and cut off brown, hollow, or rotted roots.
Dust the base with fungicide powder or ground cinnamon and allow it to dry in shade for 3–4 days.
Replant in dry, mineral-heavy succulent mix in a porous terracotta pot.
Do not water for 10 days to encourage thick new root tips to emerge.

common_problems.problem: Leaf browning and sun stress (Excess direct summer sun)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the dark green leaves turning reddish-brown, dry, or curling inward at the pointed tips?
solve_it_like_this: Shift the pot away from harsh direct sunlight to a location with bright, dappled or indirect light.
Water adequately once the soil has dried out to relieve heat dehydration.
Leaves will revert from reddish-brown to rich deep green within 2 to 3 weeks of milder lighting.

common_problems.problem: Foliage shriveling and flattening (Dehydration or dead root system)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the normally plump, ridged leaves looking deflated, thin, and concave?
solve_it_like_this: Check soil moisture: if dry for weeks, give a thorough bottom-soak in a tray of water for 30 minutes.
If the soil is already damp but the leaves are still shriveled, the roots have likely rotted away; inspect roots and re-root in pumice.
Provide bright indirect light and maintain good airflow.

common_problems.problem: Mealybugs (Nesting deep between rigid pointed leaves)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see white waxy cotton spots or sticky honeydew secreted deep within the leaf crevices?
solve_it_like_this: Use a toothpick or cotton swab soaked in isopropyl alcohol to physically remove bugs from narrow leaf joints.
Spray thoroughly with diluted neem oil soap solution in the early morning.
Inspect roots during repotting for subterranean root mealybugs.

watering_every_days.note: Gasteria has thick, leathery tongue-shaped leaves that hold extensive water reserves. Soak the potting mix thoroughly, then allow it to dry out almost completely before re-watering. Protect from continuous rain in the monsoon to avoid fungal leaf spotting.

soil.in_simple_words: Highly porous, airy succulent potting mix containing gravel, pumice, and sand with minimal organic matter.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts coarse sand or pumice + 1 part perlite + 1 part garden soil + 1 part vermicompost

pet_and_child_safety.note: Considered non-toxic and pet-safe for cats, dogs, and children. Produces no irritating sap, toxins, or spines.

common_problems.problem: Black fungal leaf spot (High humidity and poor ventilation)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are there small, sunken black or dark brown spots developing across the mottled surface of the tongue-shaped leaves?
solve_it_like_this: Relocate the plant immediately to a brighter, well-ventilated spot with active air movement.
Keep leaves strictly dry when watering; never mist or allow rainwater to pool on foliage.
Treat with a copper-based or systemic carbendazim/mancozeb fungicide spray (2 g/L) once every 10 days.

common_problems.problem: Sun scorch and stress pigmentation (Harsh direct sunlight)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the mottled green strap leaves turning dull yellow, dark purple-brown, or developing bleached patches?
solve_it_like_this: Shift the plant out of direct midday sun; Gasteria naturally grows in the dappled shade of scrub shrubs.
Provide bright, indirect daylight or gentle morning sunlight only.
Normal green colouration will return once lighting intensity is lowered.

common_problems.problem: Basal rot (Excess moisture in dense soil)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the base of the plant turning soft, dark brown, and smelly, causing outer leaves to detach effortlessly?
solve_it_like_this: Unpot the plant, slice away all rotted tissue with a sanitized knife, and treat wounds with cinnamon or fungicide.
Let the plant dry out in a cool, shaded area for 5–7 days before repotting in gritty gravel-rich mix.
Switch to a terracotta pot with ample drainage holes.

common_problems.problem: Loss of leaf patterns and pale growth (Deep indoor shade)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are new leaves coming out abnormally long, floppy, pale green, and lacking distinct white tubercles or mottling?
solve_it_like_this: Move the plant closer to an east- or north-facing window with strong ambient daylight.
Wipe dust off leaves monthly with a damp cloth so photosynthesis is maximized.
Avoid over-fertilising in low light conditions.

watering_every_days.note: Inspect the spherical pearls: water only when the translucent epidermal window slits close up and the pearls slightly soften or puckering occurs. Water from below (bottom-watering) or gently around the edge. In monsoon, keep sheltered completely from rain; excess humidity and wet soil turn the pearl beads to mush within 48 hours.

soil.in_simple_words: Extremely porous, lightweight gritty mix in a shallow terracotta hanging pot with multiple drainage holes.
soil.mix_recipe: 3 parts pumice or perlite + 2 parts coarse sand + 1 part cocopeat + 1 part vermicompost

pet_and_child_safety.note: Toxic to cats, dogs, and humans. Curio rowleyanus contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids that can cause drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, and potential liver damage if eaten. The plant sap can also cause contact dermatitis.

common_problems.problem: Mushy, translucent pearl beads (Overwatering and poor aeration)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the spherical beads turning yellow, translucent, soft, and bursting into mush?
solve_it_like_this: Stop watering immediately and move the pot to a well-ventilated, bright spot with active air circulation.
Carefully snip off rotting strands before the rot travels up the stem to the root crown.
Take healthy green stem cuttings and coil them over dry gritty soil to re-root new strands.
Switch to bottom-watering only when the pearls show slight wrinkling.

common_problems.problem: Wrinkled, flattened pearls (Underwatering and root dehydration)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the beads looking shrunken, raisin-like, and deflated, with dull green color?
solve_it_like_this: Place the shallow pot in a tray with 2–3 cm of room-temperature water for 20–30 minutes until moisture wicks up to the surface.
Empty the drainage tray thoroughly so the pot never sits in stagnant water.
Pearls will re-plump into firm, shiny spheres within 24 to 48 hours.

common_problems.problem: Crown rot at soil line (Overhead watering and damp pot top)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the stems rotting right where they rest on the soil surface while the trailing tips look temporarily green?
solve_it_like_this: Top-dress the soil surface with a 1 cm layer of coarse pumice or gravel so trailing stems do not touch moist organic soil.
Avoid pouring water directly over the crown of the pot.
Ensure the pot is made of porous terracotta and not glazed ceramic or plastic.

common_problems.problem: Sparse, leggy strings (Insufficient lighting)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are trailing stems spindly and thin with tiny pearls spaced far apart, leaving the top of the pot bald?
solve_it_like_this: Hang the pot where the top of the pot receives bright indirect light or 2–3 hours of gentle morning sun.
Loop trailing strands back onto the bare soil surface and pin them down with bobby pins; they will root at nodes and fill out the top.
Avoid placing in dark corners or deep indoor shade.

watering_every_days.note: Features bead-like aerial and underground tubers that store moisture. Water thoroughly only when the top 50–70% of the soil has dried out and leaves feel soft and pliable to a gentle pinch (the 'taco test'). In monsoon, maintain high airflow and water sparingly to avoid tuber rot.

soil.in_simple_words: Airy, well-aerated chunky succulent mix that does not compact around fragile tubers and fine roots.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts coarse sand or perlite + 2 parts cocopeat/leaf mold + 1 part pumice or orchid bark + 1 part vermicompost

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic to cats, dogs, and humans (verified by ASPCA). Safe for hanging in high-traffic living areas, balconies, or homes with pets.

common_problems.problem: Tuber and stem rot (Excessive watering and dense soggy potting mix)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are heart-shaped leaves turning yellow, translucent, and dropping, with tubers softening into mush?
solve_it_like_this: Stop watering immediately and check tubers at the soil surface; discard mushy, rotten tubers.
Take healthy stem cuttings with intact tubers or leaf pairs, let them air dry for a day, and lay them on moist vermiculite or sphagnum moss to root.
Ensure potting mix contains 50% coarse mineral grit like perlite or pumice.

common_problems.problem: Pale leaves and long internodes (Insufficient light)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are heart leaves spaced far apart on pale wire-like stems, losing their silvery pattern and purple underside hue?
solve_it_like_this: Relocate the hanging pot to receive plenty of bright, filtered daylight with 2–3 hours of gentle morning sun.
Bright light intensifies leaf marbling and vibrant rosy-purple pigmentation on stem vines.
Prune spindly vines to promote bushier new growth from the base.

common_problems.problem: Tangled hanging vines (Wind or physical handling snarls)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Have multiple trailing vines knotted together into an intractable bird's nest of stems?
solve_it_like_this: Lay the hanging pot on a flat table and use a pair of chopsticks or your fingers to gently separate vines from top to bottom.
Prune out severely tangled knots and propagate the cuttings back into the pot.
Hang away from gusty balcony winds and drafty air conditioner vents.

common_problems.problem: Thin, curled, papery leaves (Severe underwatering)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are heart leaves curling inwards, feeling thin and papery rather than firm and succulent?
solve_it_like_this: Give the plant a deep, thorough watering until water drains generously from the bottom holes.
Ensure the soil wicks moisture and hasn't shrunk into a hydrophobic brick.
Leaves will plump up and firm up within 24 to 36 hours after watering.

watering_every_days.note: The densely packed cylindrical leaves hold extensive moisture reserves. Water thoroughly only when the soil is completely dry and the oldest leaves near the soil base start to feel slightly soft or deflated. During heavy Indian monsoons, place under shelter; rain-drenched soil causes plump leaves to burst, turn yellow-translucent, and detach easily.

soil.in_simple_words: Super gritty, fast-draining cactus and succulent mix in a sturdy terracotta pot or hanging basket that won't hold damp soil.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts coarse sand or fine gravel + 2 parts perlite/pumice + 1 part garden soil + 1 part vermicompost

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic to dogs, cats, and humans (verified by ASPCA). Perfectly safe around pets and children, though hanging it out of the path of curious paws and wagging tails prevents delicate leaves from getting knocked off.

common_problems.problem: Excessive leaf shedding (Physical handling or moisture stress)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are plump jelly-bean leaves falling off in large numbers at the slightest bump or watering session?
solve_it_like_this: Hang the plant in a permanent, undisturbed location protected from foot traffic, pets, and strong winds.
Gently gather fallen healthy plump leaves and lay them horizontally on dry succulent soil; they will produce new plantlets in 3–4 weeks.
Avoid moving or rotating the pot unnecessarily.

common_problems.problem: Translucent mushy leaves and stem rot (Overwatering)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves turning yellowish-white, translucent, soft, and falling off, revealing blackened decaying stems?
solve_it_like_this: Withhold watering immediately and ensure drainage holes are completely unblocked.
Cut the stem above the rotted area with a sterile blade, let the stem cutting callus for 4 days, and replant in completely dry gritty mix.
Never let the pot sit in standing drainage saucer water.

common_problems.problem: Etiolation and sparse leaf spacing (Inadequate sunlight)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are cascading stems growing thin and pale green, with wide bare gaps between the plump leaves instead of dense, overlapping ropes?
solve_it_like_this: Move the plant to a brighter location receiving 4–5 hours of gentle morning sun or bright filtered terrace light.
Protect from intense direct summer afternoon sun which can bleach foliage.
New growth will become densely stacked and exhibit the characteristic silvery-blue powdery hue.

common_problems.problem: Mealybug infestation (Hidden in tight leaf joints)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you notice white cotton-like fluff and sticky secretions wedged tightly between the overlapping leaves?
solve_it_like_this: Apply 70% isopropyl alcohol using a fine mist sprayer or dab carefully with a cotton bud to dissolve mealybugs without knocking off leaves.
Spray early morning with diluted insecticidal soap or mild neem oil solution.
Isolate the plant until the infestation is completely resolved.
